service.description: What the database db allows the Tools screens, and why the rest is not available ("needs the pg_monitor role", "pg_stat_statements is not loaded"), probed once and kept five minutes; refresh probes again. features maps each of statementStats, activity, cancel, terminate, lockWaits, tableSizes, bloatExact, indexUsage, indexOnline, fkLightLock, maintenance, integrity, settings, settingsEdit and backups to available and reason (why not, or what limits it). backend is embedded-postgres, postgres, mysql or mariadb. available is false, with reason, when the database did not answer.

Forget the entity facade's statement stats of this instance (entity-facade@query-stats), as ec.entity.clearQueryStats() does. Needs the DATABASE_ADMIN permission, and writes a DbaStatsReset DatabaseAudit row.

The statements of sqlText as a run with Allow Changes needs them confirmed: each with changes (it may change data), ownTransaction (VACUUM, CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY, CREATE DATABASE: runs on its own), implicitCommit (MySQL DDL, which commits) and transactionControl; changeCount; and token, the one-time confirmation run#Sql or explain#Sql takes for this user, db and sqlText on any instance, good for ten minutes (moqui.database.SqlRunToken). On a production instance confirmDatabaseName is the name run#Sql needs typed. parameterNames are the :name parameters. Transaction control (COMMIT, ROLLBACK, BEGIN, SAVEPOINT, SET TRANSACTION, MySQL LOCK TABLES, SET autocommit, ...) is refused in every mode: a run is its own transaction.

Run sqlText, split into statements. Read only unless allowChanges, which needs the token of classify#Sql (spent by this run) and on production confirmDatabaseName. With changes the script is one transaction and stops at the first failure (rolledBack), unless eachOnOwn; a read-only script stops at its first failure too. parameters binds each :name as a value. limit rows per query (500, at most 100,000); offset fetches more of a single read-only query; timeoutSeconds (300, at most 3,600) cancels the statement running at the time. runId (8 to 36 letters, digits or -) names the run for cancel#SqlRun; one is made when empty, and one running on any instance is refused. A cancel or timeout with statements left rolls a transaction back. Every connection a run with changes used is closed after it, so no session state reaches later work. results has, per statement: seq, sql, givesRows, columns, records (lists of values), limitReached, rowsAffected, durationMs, error, rerunnable (a plain query run read only: may be run again to sort, filter or fetch more), skipped, rolledBack (it ran and was rolled back) and auditId. A refused attempt with changes (no or a spent token, the wrong name) is audited too.

Cancel the run runId: the user's own, or any with DATABASE_ADMIN. On this instance through its connection's canceller; a run on another instance is found by its running audit row and cancelled with pg_cancel_backend or KILL QUERY, once the session is checked to be the one the row recorded (Postgres backend_start, MySQL the server's start); a running row older than the longest timeout is ignored. outcome is cancelled, cancelledRemote (with instanceId and backendId) or notRunning. Refused under the read fence for a remote cancel. Writes a DbaCancel audit row.

The plan of one statement (§7.5): Postgres EXPLAIN (FORMAT JSON, VERBOSE, BUFFERS), MySQL and MariaDB EXPLAIN FORMAT=JSON. analyze runs it: Postgres adds ANALYZE, MySQL EXPLAIN ANALYZE (format text), MariaDB ANALYZE FORMAT=JSON. A statement that may change data then needs the token of classify#Sql (and on production confirmDatabaseName) and runs in a transaction that is rolled back (rolledBack), as every analyzed statement on MySQL and MariaDB does. Registered under runId for cancel#SqlRun, under timeoutSeconds as run#Sql. plan is the database's text (JSON when format is json).

The SQL editor's completion schema: tables (table name to its column names, a table outside the connection's schema as schema.table), entities (each entity of the group to its table) and dialect (postgres or mysql).

The database's own statement stats (§7.2), the most costly first, at most limit (100, at most 1,000). Postgres pg_stat_statements: query_id, query, calls, total_exec_time, mean_exec_time, rows, shared_blks_hit, shared_blks_read, temp_blks_written (milliseconds). MySQL and MariaDB events_statements_summary_by_digest: query_id, query, calls, sum_timer_wait (picoseconds), sum_rows_examined, sum_no_index_used. When they do not read, available is false with the reason of get#Capabilities.
Reset the database's own statement stats: pg_stat_statements_reset(), or a TRUNCATE of the digest table. Needs DATABASE_ADMIN; refused under the read fence; writes a DbaStatsReset audit row.

The current user's own SQL audit rows, newest first (limit 50, at most 500), of db when given: the SQL screen's history. Each has auditId, db, statementText, isChange, rowsReturned, rowsAffected, durationMs, errorText and startTime.
The user's own saved queries and the shared ones (of db when given), by description: queryId, description, db, sqlText, ownerUserId, isShared, parametersJson.
Create a saved query (no queryId), owned by the current user, or update one the user owns. parametersJson, when given, is JSON (the :name parameters' defaults).
Delete a saved query the current user owns.

Delete the DatabaseAudit rows older than the database_audit_days property (90 by default, at least 1), and the expired SqlRunToken rows: the DatabaseAuditPurge ServiceJob, which runs with no user signed in; a signed-in caller needs DATABASE_ADMIN.

The grid's columns, each: name, title, type (text, long-text, number, date, time, date-time, indicator, boolean, binary), editable, editor (input, textarea, number, date, time, datetime, tickCross, list; null when not editable), pk, encrypted (shown masked, never edited), notNull, createOnly, maxLength, relatedEntity and relatedField (the lookup's), and field (an editable SQL result's entity field). entityName is the entity the grid saves to: the source's, or a SQL result's whose columns are all of one table with its entity's whole primary key (§9.5); null when read only, with readOnlyReason. hasStamp: each row has _stamp, which save sends back.

One page for Tabulator's progressive load: page from 1, size (100, at most 1,000). last_page is page plus one while pages come back full, and the page itself once one is short, with last_row the row count then; no count is run. For an unfiltered entity source last_row is the catalog's estimate while more pages come (estimated true). Each row of data is a map of the columns; an entity row has its primary key and _stamp (its lastUpdatedStamp) too; encrypted fields are masked.
Count rows: an entity find count, or count(*) over the wrapped SQL, with the source's conditions and filter.

The whole source (conditions, filter, sort, columns) as format csv (default) or xlsx, written to location (a dbresource:// location, or under runtime://tmp/ or runtime://export/), or when empty to a new location under runtime://tmp/grid-export/ that the screen sends as a download. An entity source is read through the find's cursor and CSV written row by row; XLSX is built in memory and stops at 100,000 rows; a SQL source stops at 200,000 rows; truncated says so. Encrypted fields are masked.

The options of a related-entity column (field of entityName, whose one relationship has it as the single key): the related rows whose key or label holds term, ignoring case, 20 at a time from offset. Each option has value and label (the related entity's description, else a ...Name field, with the key).

Save the grid's changes to entityName in one transaction: updates [{pk, stamp, fields}] (only the edited fields), creates [{fields}], deletes [{pk, stamp}], each through the entity's update#, create# or delete# (its authorization, validation, ECA rules and audit log apply). stamp is the row's _stamp; a row changed since is refused (conflict, "changed by someone else since you loaded it"). Every row is checked before any is written; a refused row rolls back every other. saved is true only when everything was saved; refused lists each refused row: kind (update, create, delete), index (in its list), pk, message, fieldErrors (field to message) and conflict. Views, the identity and secret entities, UserAccount's secret fields, encrypted fields, key fields of an update and lastUpdatedStamp are refused. Writes a DbaGridSave audit row with the entity and the counts, not the values.
The user's own grid views and the shared ones, by description: viewId, description, ownerUserId, isShared, sourceJson, layoutJson.
Create a grid view (no viewId), owned by the current user, or update one the user owns. sourceJson (required) and layoutJson (columns, widths, order, frozen, filters, sort) are JSON.
Delete a grid view the current user owns.
